entities.summary: Cao Cao (b. 155 CE, Buzhou) was a key figure in the late Eastern Han dynasty of China, a period marked by internal strife, regional warlords, and eventual division into three kingdoms. Cao Cao's strategic alliances and military campaigns led to the establishment of the Cao Wei kingdom, which would eventually succeed the Han dynasty and shape the course of Chinese history. His legacy extended beyond his own reign, as he influenced the development of Confucianism and the arts, and his court attracted scholars, poets, and artists from across the empire. The Cao Wei kingdom, founded by Cao Cao, would go on to play a crucial role in the reunification of China under the Jin dynasty in 280 CE. As Cao Cao's own empire crumbled, his adopted son Cao Pi would succeed him, marking the beginning of a new era in Chinese history. Cao Cao's impact on Chinese politics, culture, and society cannot be overstated, as he played a pivotal role in shaping the future of the Chinese empire.
